what_happened: On 2026-10-31 the the person running Athena re-tiered the whole queue by hand after Sri said everything can't be urgent. The queue had 13 urgent and 14 high items, so priority no longer ordered anything. The the person running Athena kept three items urgent (anbv, b5hm, c5yx) and the rest of the speed work high. They moved 13 other urgent or high items to normal, set 7ym7 (Hestia's re-queue of the already closed gdgv) to low, and closed vn3s because hydf had already done it. This was a hand intervention outside any job.
cause: Athena sets no limit on how many items can hold the urgent or high tier and does not check that the tiers still separate work. Whoever files a request, a person or another agent such as Hestia, can pick any priority at no cost, and nothing asks for a reason or demotes it later. Nothing checks new items against closed or finished work, so a re-queue of a closed job (7ym7 for gdgv) and a finished item (vn3s) stayed queued. Only a person noticing that the queue had become unordered would trigger a cleanup.
prevention: Add a queue check that runs at enqueue and on every drain. It would (1) cap the urgent tier at a small configured number, for example 3, and the high tier at a configured share of the queue, and refuse the excess with a message naming the current holders; (2) require a one-line reason for urgent; (3) flag any queued item that re-asks a closed job or whose work already landed, and hold it for retirement. `athena queue` would also show tier counts and warn near a cap.
proposed_request: Keep queue priority meaningful. Outcome: the urgent and high tiers can never again fill up so that priority stops ordering work. Add configured caps in athena.toml for how many queued items may be urgent (default 3) and high (default a set share of the queue). Enqueueing an item that would exceed a cap is refused with a message naming the current holders, unless the caller demotes one. Urgent requires a one-line reason, which is stored with the item. On enqueue and on each drain, flag queued items that re-ask a closed job or whose deliverable has already landed, and hold them for retirement instead of running them. `athena queue` shows tier counts and warns when a cap is near. Acceptance: tests show an enqueue over the urgent cap is refused, an urgent item without a reason is refused, a re-queue of a closed job is flagged and held, and queues under the caps behave as before. Replay the new refusals against past real queue entries to confirm ordinary requests are not refused.
